hints: As you walk the array, what do you need to remember to notice that a value has turned up before?
Keep a hash set of values already seen. The moment you meet a value that is already in the set, a repeat exists.

1. Read N and the values.
  2. Start an empty set.
  3. For each value: if it is in the set, the answer is YES.
  4. Otherwise add it to the set.
  5. If the loop ends with no hit, print NO.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Compare every pair of positions for equal values.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Sort the array; any repeat ends up next to its twin, so check neighbours.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One pass with a HashSet; add returning false means the value was already there.

explain: For 1 2 3 1 the set grows to {1, 2, 3}. When the last 1 arrives it is already in the set, so we print YES. In Java, set.add(x) returns false when x was present, which gives the check for free. Values go up to 109 in size, so a counting array will not work; a hash set handles any range.
recognize: "Does anything appear twice?" → remember what you have seen in a hash set.
python:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
vals = data[1:1 + n]
print("YES" if len(set(vals)) < n else "NO")  # fewer distinct values means a repeat
